# Artifact

!`atlas publish --target export --page dashboard --out .atlas/artifact-page.html --no-color`

> **If the block above is empty**, `atlas` is not on `PATH` — the plugin is not installed where this is
> running. Say so; do not read an empty section as "the export produced nothing".

---

`atlas publish --target export` has already run. It wrote a **self-contained** page — one file, every
stylesheet and script inlined, no external request — with `stripLocalOnly` applied and `assertNoLocalOnly`
verifying its own output.

**There is no `atlas artifact` command, deliberately.** Everything the CLI needed to do here it already did
for `--target export`; adding a second command over the same code would be two names for one thing, which is
the duplication this tool exists to detect. What the CLI *cannot* do is reach claude.ai — only a session can.
That gap is this skill, and it is the whole of it.

## Publish it

Call the **Artifact** tool with the file the block above named:

- `file_path` — the path it wrote, normally `.atlas/artifact-page.html`
- `title` — the repository name and the page, e.g. `project-atlas · Overview`
- `description` — one sentence: what the page shows and that it is derived from the repository's own markdown
- `favicon` — a single emoji, and **the same one every time you republish this page**; a changed icon reads
  as a different artifact to someone looking for a tab

**To update a page published earlier, pass its `url`.** Publishing without it creates a *second* artifact
rather than updating the first, and the reader keeps the old link. If you do not have the URL, find it with
`action: "list"` or ask. Redeploying from the same `file_path` inside one session updates in place.

## Before you publish — check, do not assume

The export strips local-only panels and asserts its own output, so the boundary is held in code rather than
by this instruction. Confirm the line saying so appeared, and then:

- **Say what is going out.** The size and which page. A reader deciding whether to share something is
  entitled to know what it contains before it has a URL.
- **An artifact is private to the user until they share it** — say that, because "publish" sounds like it
  is not. What it is *not* is local: it leaves this machine.
- **Never publish a page the export refused.** If `assertNoLocalOnly` threw, stop and report it. That guard
  exists because the stripper once failed open and returned a document unchanged, and a private task list
  and every uncommitted path went out through four exit doors. This is a fifth door.

## Which page

Default is the dashboard. Re-run the command with `--page health` or `--page index` if the user asked for
one of those — the health report is the better share when the question is "is this corpus in good shape",
the index when it is "what documentation exists".

`--target export` also takes `--all`, which writes `all.standalone.html` — every page in one file with a
nav. Offer it when they want the whole site rather than one screen, and say it is larger.

## What not to do

- **Do not publish a filesystem path or a `127.0.0.1` URL.** A loopback dashboard is not shareable; that is
  the point of this command.
- **Do not publish anything else in the repository** — not the journal, not `.atlas/` state, not a worklog.
  This skill publishes one generated page.
- **Do not re-strip or post-process the HTML yourself.** It is already correct, and a second pass over it is
  a second implementation of the boundary.
